newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil up on fresh buying.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Fuel oil up on fresh buying.

text.p: Singapore fuel oil swaps firmed late afternoon on Tuesday on fresh buying after more than two weeks of lacklustre trading as players looked to renewed trading interest in the local physical market, traders said.
"Fuel oil is firming because of some buying from a few traders and there are talks that physical buyers will emerge later today," one trader said.
May fuel oil swaps were last quoted at $96.50/$97.50 per barrel, up from Monday's $95.50/$96.50, brokers said. It was quoted down to an intra-day low of $95.25/$96.25 this morning, they said.
Brokers said May traded earlier in the day at $96.25 and $96.50 per tonne while balance April traded at $97.10.
Trading on the local physical market has thin over the past two weeks as players were sidelined due to thin cargo demand and reduced bunker sales.
Traders said the market is picking up because signs are emerging of renewed buying interest from China which had more than halved its monthly purchases since late January.
Others said that demand from Singapore will also pick up for both cargo and bunker as South Korea begins their spring refinery maintenance programme.
Gas oil swaps extended its directionless early day trade to drift down slightly as players await fresh physical direction.
May gas oil swaps were last quoted down about 20 cents from Monday at $25.60/$25.75 per barrel, brokers said.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread (regrade) widened on the strength of the gas oil market and the relative weakness of jet fuel demand.
Brokers said May regrade traded earlier in the day at minus 50 cents down from Monday's 40 cents traded level.
May regrade was last quoted at -60/-40 cents from Monday's -40/-20 cents, they said.
